mine: before God; the one whom God declares guilty
note: Again ha-elohim / elohim (with plural verb yarshi'un); best read as God giving a verdict at the sanctuary rather than a panel of judges (KJV 22:9).
mohar is the price paid by the groom to the bride's father, not a dowry brought by the bride (KJV 22:17).
mekhashefah is a female practitioner of sorcery or magic; "witch" carries later European associations that shaped how the verse was used (KJV 22:18).
neshekh is any interest on a loan, not only excessive interest as "usury" now means (KJV 22:25).

elohim here is most naturally "God" (paired with the human chief, nasi); KJV's "the gods" (or judges) follows a traditional reading (KJV 22:28). Context: God (medium confidence). Elohim with a singular sense is normal, and the pairing with the human chief (nasi) sets divine and human authority side by side. ESV, NIV, NASB, NRSV, NJPS, CSB and NET read 'God'. Acts 23:5 quotes only the second line. Other possible meanings: (1) 'the gods' (do not revile other peoples' gods) — LXX theous, Vulgate diis, Philo, Josephus, KJV; (2) 'the judges' — Targum Onkelos (dayyana), Mekhilta, Rashi, cf. 21:6.
